equity_bridge.item: Investments accounted for using the equity method (49% Xinyi Solar (Tianjin) 174MW, Malaysia 100MW JV) at book
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet; share of results sits below EBITDA so the asset enters the bridge (matching-asset rule)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run base-path growth after the 2025 Reform Notice; the FY2023-FY2025 equity CAGR (4.5%) was funded by RMB4.6bn of parent-sourced acquisitions that stopped in H1 FY2026 and is not extrapolated
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR 4.5% vs EPS CAGR 2.6% and revenue 3.7% over FY2023-FY2025 (>30% relative gap): book value grew through retained earnings and scrip dividends while per-share earnings barely moved -- returns on the new capital are falling.
historical_growth.notes: CAGR basis is FY2023->FY2025 (two years, RMB-restated), the only span in the continuing reporting currency; FY2019-FY2022 were reported in HKD and are not converted, so 5-year fields are null. Owner FCF was negative in FY2023 (-1,694) and FY2024 (-1,345) from acquisition capex, so an FCF CAGR is undefined; H1 FY2026 owner FCF of RMB334m (vs RMB120m in H1 FY2025) reflects the acquisition pause, not operating improvement -- revenue fell 13.1% and net profit 28.9%.

scenario_narratives.base: A structurally lower-margin, roughly flat business. The June-2025 Reform Notice ended guaranteed fixed tariffs for new projects and moved existing capacity toward 'mechanism tariff + market price'; the H1 FY2026 result (revenue -13.1%, gross margin 51.7% vs 61.8%) is the new run-rate, not a cyclical trough. Revenue steps down ~15% over FY2026-27 and then grows 0-2% as ~100MW/yr of selective, return-tested acquisitions from Xinyi Solar offset FiT roll-off. Reported EBITDA margins hold ~86-88% on a fixed-cost asset base; cash conversion is haircut 6pp fading to 3pp for the RMB4.2bn subsidy-receivable build. Cash tax ramps to 25% as tax holidays expire. Capex rises toward 18% of revenue to fund repowering at today's panel costs; the terminal value is capped at 11x FCF for a finite-life portfolio.
scenario_narratives.bull: The acquisition pipeline reopens (~200MW/yr from FY2027), curtailment eases on the green-electricity quota and grid investment, mechanism tariffs settle near legacy levels, and the MoF settles subsidy arrears so operating cash converts at ~100% of EBITDA. Revenue regains its FY2025 level by FY2029 and compounds 3-6% thereafter; EBITDA margin recovers to 88.5%; terminal 12x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Curtailment and spot-market prices deteriorate toward the independent estimates, the parent stops selling assets, FiT entitlements roll off with nothing replacing them, and subsidy arrears keep absorbing cash. Revenue falls ~27% by FY2030 and stays there; EBITDA margin (cash basis) 70%; D&A stays fixed so EBIT margin halves; terminal 9x on a zero-growth stream.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Xinyi Energy as a finite-life, policy-exposed cash-flow stream rather than as a growth IPP: the FY2023-FY2025 earnings growth was bought from the parent with debt and has stopped, and the 2025 tariff reform plus curtailment reset margins structurally. The model discounts unlevered, cash-conversion-adjusted owner FCF at a CNY-built 7% WACC, deducts bank debt and land leases, adds the equity-accounted Tianjin and Malaysia stakes at book, caps the terminal multiple for asset life, and converts to HKD at the dated CNY/HKD rate. The result is a wide bear-to-bull range whose weighted centre is what matters.
key_risks_to_valuation: Curtailment: a move from the official ~8.6% toward independent ~26% estimates is the single largest lever on revenue and sits in the bear case.
Mechanism-tariff bidding outcomes by province through 2026-27 set the post-FiT price level; the base assumes a further ~3% revenue step-down in FY2027.
Subsidy receivables (RMB4.2bn): settlement would add up to ~RMB0.49/share (HKD0.58) of cash the model only partly credits; continued build is the bear haircut.
Parent behaviour: Xinyi Solar controls deal flow, pricing of connected transactions and the board; the base assumes only ~100MW/yr of acquisitions.
Finite asset life: the 11x terminal cap and rising replacement capex are judgments; a 14x Gordon multiple would add ~20% to the base value.
FX: a 5% RMB depreciation against the HKD peg moves every HKD per-share value by 5%; the rate is dated 2026-10-22 and refresh_price.py does not update it.
WACC: a CNY WACC of 6-8% is defensible; each 1pp is roughly 15% of base value on a terminal-heavy stream.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 0.69-1.40 HKD. CNY/HKD from Yahoo CNYHKD=X same date.
data_sources.financials: 3868.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2023-FY2025 and H1 FY2024-H1 FY2026 in RMB; FY2019-FY2022 in HKD not used), H1 FY2026 interim report (balance sheet, borrowings note 15, receivables note 12, EPS note 9), FY2025 annual report (cash flow, lease and ROU notes).
data_sources.qualitative: 3868.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-23): Reform Notice, curtailment estimates, acquisition pause, Tianjin deconsolidation, NZ acquisition, infrastructure-fund plan.

inputs.share_count_basis: 8,519.712m weighted shares in issue at 30 June 2026 plus 0.22m dilutive share options (H1 FY2026 interim note 9(b)); held FLAT. The count has grown ~1.3%/yr FY2023-FY2026 through scrip dividends, which is non-SBC issuance in lieu of cash dividends; in an unlevered DCF the cash retained offsets the dilution, so no share growth is charged.
inputs.sbc_source: Share option expense in the condensed cash flow statement: RMB0.09m H1 FY2025, RMB0.23m H1 FY2026 (interim reports). FY2025 full year taken as ~RMB0.2m. SBC-zero market: projected at 0% of revenue and the house/street band collapses.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (reporting currency changed from HKD to RMB with the FY2024 annual report; FY2023 restated). HKEX quote in HKD. All per-share values computed in CNY then converted at CNY/HKD 1.1734 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22; inverse HKDCNY=X 0.8513 -> 1/0.8513 = 1.1747, ties within the spread). Direction: IV_HKD = IV_CNY x 1.1734. No dual listing exists for a parity check; the interim dividend is declared in HK cents on an RMB profit, which is the same direction.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 interim: bank borrowings RMB4,561.7m non-current + RMB2,185.1m current = RMB6,746.8m (unsecured, 2.42% weighted rate, mostly floating); lease liabilities RMB925.3m + RMB80.7m = RMB1,006.0m (solar-farm land leases); less cash RMB780.0m (restricted cash RMB8.4m excluded). Net debt RMB6,972.9m. The company's own 'net debt' of RMB5,966.8m excludes leases; this model includes them (treatment A). Amounts due to parent are nil since FY2023.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. CoE 9.5% = CNY 10y risk-free 1.8% + beta 1.1 x China ERP 7.0% (country risk inside the ERP). After-tax cost of debt 3.0%: the current 2.42% floating onshore rate is a cyclical low, normalised to 4.0% pre-tax at 25%. Target weights 55% equity / 45% debt (book net gearing 45-48%; market-value weights are distorted by a depressed equity) -> 6.6%, rounded to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: policy, curtailment and controlling-shareholder risk are charged once, in the flows and the scenario weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. RMB1,006.0m lease liabilities (land under the solar farms) sit in net debt; lease principal (RMB70.9m FY2025) is NOT deducted from flows; EBITDA is post-IFRS-16 as reported; D&A includes right-of-use depreciation (RMB50.4m FY2025) and is added back, so the lease asset is funded by the liability in the bridge, charged once. Sanity multiples are therefore lease-inclusive EV against post-IFRS-16 EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (RMB -0.4m FY2025, nil FY2024 after the NCI buy-out) and ignored; flows are treated as fully attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: non-US operating company with leases and a reporting/quote currency split; adaptations file read). Xinyi Energy is a solar/wind independent power producer, not a REIT or utility with a regulated asset base, so a going-concern cash-flow model fits; the finite life of the farms (25-30 yrs, average age ~6-7 yrs) is handled by capping the terminal multiple at 9-12x and by raising capex toward replacement levels in the outer years rather than by a Gordon perpetuity at the WACC. NOT Xinyi Glass (0868.HK); parent is Xinyi Solar (0968.HK). CASH CONVERSION: EBITDA margins in assumptions are CASH-conversion-adjusted, not the reported ~88% (H1 FY2026 88.6%, FY2025 96.6%). Tariff-adjustment (subsidy) receivables are RMB4,209.6m at 30 June 2026 (1.7x annual revenue, 4.6 years of subsidy income) and still rising (+RMB214m in six months); cash generated from operations was only 74% of EBITDA over FY2023-H1 FY2026. The base case carries a 6pp haircut to the reported margin fading to 3pp by year 10 as the FiT share of revenue shrinks; bear 8-10pp persistent; bull 3pp fading to zero (arrears settlement would be upside). The tax line is computed on the haircut EBIT, which understates cash tax by ~1pp of revenue; accepted and noted. INTEREST INCOME not stripped (RMB3.1m, company is net debt). The RMB506.8m equity-accounted investments (49% of Xinyi Solar (Tianjin) retained after the Dec-2025 deconsolidation, plus the 100MW Malaysia JV) earn below EBITDA, so they are added in the bridge at book under the matching-asset rule. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 649.64 - SBC 0.2 - interest income 0 = 649.4 (OCF 1,651.0 less capex 1,001.4, where capex is almost entirely the 230MW '2025 Portfolio' bought from Xinyi Solar; maintenance capex is ~1-2% of revenue). Historical reported FCF was negative FY2023-FY2024 because of acquisition capex (RMB2.3bn/yr), not operating weakness; the engine projects capex explicitly so the historical FCF CAGR is not used for growth selection.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: Engine flows are unlevered (pre-interest). Reported FCF is after RMB218m interest paid, so year-1 unlevered FCF (~RMB1.3bn) is above last_fcf by roughly interest paid plus the step-down in acquisition capex; this is expected, not a one-off being carried forward.

bear.narrative: Curtailment moves toward the independent ~26% estimate rather than the official 8.6%, spot-market clearing prices stay low or negative in oversupplied provinces, mechanism-tariff bids come in well below legacy FiT levels, the parent sells nothing further and the portfolio shrinks in real terms as FiT entitlements roll off; subsidy arrears keep building (8-10pp conversion haircut), so revenue falls ~27% peak-to-trough by FY2030 against a fixed depreciation base, and the terminal multiple is 9x on a zero-growth stream.

base.growth_note: FY2026 -12%: H1 was -13.1% and H2 loses the Tianjin 174MW (deconsolidated Dec-2025) and faces the same curtailment and market-trading prices, partly offset by the full year of the 2025 Portfolio and the New Zealand services business. FY2027 -3% as mechanism-tariff bidding settles. Thereafter 0-2%: ~100MW/yr of selective acquisitions (capex 15% of revenue ~ RMB330m at RMB3.3/W) roughly offsets FiT roll-off and price drift.
base.margin_note: Reported EBITDA margin ~87.5% in FY2026 (H1 88.6%; NZ services dilution in H2) drifting to ~86%, less the subsidy-receivable cash-conversion haircut of 6pp fading to 3pp.
base.capex_note: FY2026 10% (H1 actual RMB95.6m + RMB58.8m Jinzhai wind + light H2); then 15% for selective acquisitions; rising to 18% in years 8-10 to begin funding repowering/replacement of the oldest FiT-era farms at today's ~RMB3/W (well below the RMB5-6/W book cost the 33% D&A charge reflects).
base.tax_note: Cash tax 17-24% of EBIT FY2024-H1 FY2026 as solar-farm tax holidays (3-year exemption, 3-year half rate) roll off; ramps to the 25% PRC statutory rate by year 5. PRC dividend withholding is not separately charged.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.0%/1.0% would be 16.8x FCF; capped at 11x, roughly a 20-year annuity at the WACC, matching the remaining life of a portfolio averaging ~6-7 years old. The cap binds.

bull.narrative: Acquisitions from Xinyi Solar resume at ~200MW/yr from FY2027 (capex 20-22% of revenue), the August-2026 green-electricity consumption quota and 15th Five-Year Plan grid investment ease curtailment, mechanism tariffs settle near FiT-era levels, the Malaysia JV connects on time and the NZ platform seeds a second market; subsidy arrears start to be settled so cash conversion returns to ~100%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 11x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: single-regulator exposure (every RMB of revenue depends on PRC tariff and dispatch policy, which changed structurally in 2025), a controlling-shareholder dependency for growth (zero acquisitions in H1 FY2026), and an RMB4.2bn subsidy receivable whose collection timing the company does not control. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right -- the parent resuming sales, curtailment easing, and arrears being settled. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
